Students will need to select how you wish to approach this topic, i.e. you may wish to focus on backgrounds, extra-curricular activities, relationships, or University. As a group you will select your topic and specific research question. You will add two or three questions to the skeleton interview schedule, these need to be informed by literature. You need to submit your topic and research question, and additional interview schedule questions to your individual group pages on the RMC canvas module to be approved.



























For this block of the module you will need to produce a 15-minute equivalent PowerPoint slide deck and will be invited to an online 10-minute group viva.



























This presentation will contribute 20% of the module assessment.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

This is a group effort, and a group assessment. In addition to making the poster, they also present it to their markers (two members of staff). This is normally done at a poster conference, but was done online via Teams the year this cohort did it. They have to divide the presentation up amongst group members and answer questions from their markers.

info_other1: The online tests make up what's called their 'Portfolio Mark'. This is the average of the three assessments. This portfolio mark then counts for 40% of their module mark.
tasks_other2: The students take part in group seminars where they work on a research project designed by the students and the seminar supervisor. This is a group effort, and a group assessment. In addition to making the poster, they also present it to their markers (two members of staff). This is normally done at a poster conference, but was done online via Teams the year this cohort did it. They have to divide the presentation up amongst group members and answer questions from their markers.

assess_type_other_a_specify: Online timed tests that last 1 hour.
tasks_other1:
The students took 3x online tests hosted via blackboard. They are MCQ style, but not all questions are MCQs, e.g. there are fill in the blank questions, True/False questions, run an analysis and then report the correct values. 



























The test links are available for 48 hours, and they can choose when to take the test in that timeframe. They get 1 hour to complete the test.
info_other1: The online tests make up what's called their 'Portfolio Mark'. This is the average of the three assessments. This portfolio mark then counts for 40% of their module mark.
tasks_other2: The students take part in group seminars where they work on a research project designed by the students and the seminar supervisor. The coursework component (lab report) is based on the project they do in their seminar group. In addition they make a scientific poster based on their project. This is a group effort, and a group assessment. In addition to making the poster, they also present it to their markers (two members of staff). This is normally done at a poster conference, but was done online via Teams the year this cohort did it. They have to divide the presentation up amongst group members and answer questions from their markers.
date_other2: Poster submission: 24/05/2021, Poster presentation: 26/05/2021-27/05/2021 (they were assigned a one hour slot on one of these two days).

The students took 3x online tests hosted via blackboard. They are MCQ style, but not all questions are MCQs, e.g. there are fill in the blank questions, True/False questions, run an analysis and then report the correct values. 



























The test links are available for 48 hours, and they can choose when to take the test in that timeframe. They get 1 hour to complete the test.
info_other1: The online tests make up what's called their 'Portfolio Mark'. This is the average of the three assessments. This portfolio mark then counts for 40% of their module mark.
tasks_other2: The students take part in group seminars where they work on a research project designed by the students and the seminar supervisor. The coursework component (lab report) is based on the project they do in their seminar group. In addition they make a scientific poster based on their project. This is a group effort, and a group assessment. In addition to making the poster, they also present it to their markers (two members of staff). This is normally done at a poster conference, but was done online via Teams the year this cohort did it. They have to divide the presentation up amongst group members and answer questions from their markers.
date_other2: Poster submission: 24/05/2021, Poster presentation: 26/05/2021-27/05/2021 (they were assigned a one hour slot on one of these two days).

The students took 3x online tests hosted via blackboard. They are MCQ style, but not all questions are MCQs, e.g. there are fill in the blank questions, True/False questions, run an analysis and then report the correct values. 



























The test links are available for 48 hours, and they can choose when to take the test in that timeframe. They get 1 hour to complete the test.
info_other1: The online tests make up what's called their 'Portfolio Mark'. This is the average of the three assessments. This portfolio mark then counts for 40% of their module mark.
tasks_other2: The students take part in group seminars where they work on a research project designed by the students and the seminar supervisor. The coursework component (lab report) is based on the project they do in their seminar group. In addition they make a scientific poster based on their project. This is a group effort, and a group assessment. In addition to making the poster, they also present it to their markers (two members of staff). This is normally done at a poster conference, but was done online via Teams the year this cohort did it. They have to divide the presentation up amongst group members and answer questions from their markers.
date_other2: Poster submission: 24/05/2021, Poster presentation: 26/05/2021-27/05/2021 (they were assigned a one hour slot on one of these two days).
